eras.title: Columns without a roof
eras.caption: At Chichén Itzá, ranks of stone columns remain where broad roofed spaces once stood. They show another side of the Maya city beyond its famous pyramid: gathering places built around halls, courts and carefully ordered movement.

eras.title: El Castillo across the plaza
eras.caption: El Castillo rises above the open plaza at Chichén Itzá, with nine stepped terraces and stairways leading to its summit temple. Seen from a distance, the pyramid's compact symmetry stands out against the low forest of the Yucatán plain.
eras.prompt: Chichen Itza El Castillo Temple of Kukulcan grand landscape view across wide open plaza from north-northwest at human eye height and ample distance, whole freestanding square pyramid clearly visible in three-quarter perspective. Exactly nine stepped terraces, broad steep central stair on north face with stone balustrades and small serpent heads at ground, another central stair on adjacent face, modest rectangular stone summit temple. Recognizable real proportions roughly 55 metres wide and 30 metres total height, not absurdly tall. Weathered pale grey limestone, low Yucatan forest flat horizon, foreground limestone outcrops and sparse dry grass. Main pyramid occupies middle third to half of width with space and sky around it. No invented extra temples, no mountains, no crowds or tourist ropes, no neon colors, no readable text.

evidence.basis: Interpretive study of exposed archaeological remains, sharing the existing ruin phase rather than asserting the illustrated state existed at its first year.
